label: January 5–11
title: “This Is My Work and My Glory” —  Moses 1; Abraham 3

items.text: The Bible begins with creation, but the Book of Moses and Abraham’s record shed light on what existed before. These scriptures address fundamental questions: Who is God? Who are we? What is God’s work, and what is our place in it? The Lord’s response to Moses’s plea helps frame our understanding of these profound truths.

As a child of God, you have a divine destiny. The Lord would first want you to understand your true identity. Satan, conversely, attempts to confuse you on this very point. Recognize the difference between God’s message of your divine worth and Satan’s attempts to diminish it.

The way you think about who you really are affects almost every decision you will ever make. Your identity as a child of God must precede all other labels. Consider the choices you make, prioritizing your divine heritage above all else, and live up to your eternal potential.

Powerful spiritual experiences do not guarantee freedom from temptation. Satan’s tactic is often to make us doubt these sacred moments. Learn from Moses’s example how to stay true to the testimonies you have received and resist the adversary’s influence with the Lord’s help.

Satan tempts us with counterfeits of God’s truth and power. Just as we can discern fake plants from real ones, we can learn to recognize and reject the adversary’s deceptions. Trust in the Lord’s guidance, as shown in Moses’s experience, to overcome these false offerings.

Teaching opportunities in the family frequently occur in informal, everyday moments—while eating a meal, doing chores, or traveling. These spontaneous moments are ideal for discussing how we, like Moses, can resist the influence of the adversary and choose righteousness.

After witnessing God’s creations, Moses asked, “why these things are so.” The Lord’s response reveals that His work and glory is to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man. This divine purpose underscores the infinite value of each individual soul.

The Lord declared, “This is My work and My glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.” This profound declaration reveals the ultimate purpose behind all creation and all divine action. Our eternal progression is central to God’s eternal plan.

To be “like Him” is the ultimate goal for which God created the worlds. Through His plan and the Atonement of Jesus Christ, we can overcome the Fall and gain eternal life, becoming like our Heavenly Father. This is the glorious work of our Creator.

Abraham saw our existence as spirits before the world was created. This pre-mortal life provides crucial context for understanding our divine potential and the eternal purpose of God’s plan. We were with Him before we were born, fulfilling His eternal purposes.
